in_kind_convention: MONETARY-ONLY on BOTH sides, and this filer states in-kind wholly OUTSIDE both totals — the clearest specimen of the convention in the chunk. His p7 carries a separately headed 'INKIND' table with its own From / To / Amount columns holding one line (Clear Satellite, Inc -> Regan Outdoor Advertising, 3,102.00). Adding it to either side breaks that side (contributions would miss by 3,102.22, expenditures by exactly 3,102.00); excluding it leaves expenditures EXACT and contributions off by only the traced 0.22. The in-kind line is nevertheless PUBLISHED as a contribution row flagged in_kind=true (the module's Paxman precedent: in-kind rows ride alongside the cash total, never inside it).

THE STRUCTURAL FINDING: THIS FILER DID NOT USE THE COUNTY'S SCHEDULE A / SCHEDULE B PAGES AT ALL. He filed the county cover and Summary Page and then attached his OWN typed spreadsheets — 'Joel Wright Contributions Report, Pre-Primary 2010' (Name / City / Amount / Loan) and 'Joel Wright Expenditure Report, Pre-Primary 2010' (Person or Organization / Purpose of Expenditure / Amount) — each a boxed grid ending in its own printed TOTAL. Consequences worth flagging as precedent: (a) the sides are transcribed, but there is NO county Schedule A/B page in the document and hence no 'Subtotal for this page' gate — the grand TOTAL is the only printed gate, and it holds; (b) NEITHER TABLE HAS A DATE COLUMN, so every one of the 147 rows here is honestly date-less — an absence in the document, not an unread or illegible cell, and no date was inferred from the report date; (c) the contribution table prints CITY ONLY (no street addresses anywhere), so nothing had to be withheld for privacy on this filing; (d) the typed tables are the cleanest specimen in the chunk — every figure legible at 200 dpi.
